The DFO holds the WEO's national accounts series only. Load once WEO has been chosen for an analysis, or when working with WEO figures.

debt-ids.description: Context for working with the World Bank's International Debt Statistics (IDS), the external debt of low- and middle-income countries as reported by the borrowers. Covers its sources, the debt stocks, flows, debt service, net flows and net transfers it reports and how they relate, the creditor and borrower breakdowns, the DFO's version of the data, the conversion to US dollars, projections, revisions and underreporting, how IDS differs from creditor-side data such as the CRS, and how its series codes are built. Load once IDS has been chosen for an analysis, or when working with IDS figures.
debt-ids.name: debt-ids

debt-profile.description: Context for describing a country's external debt: how much it owes and how that has changed, who borrowed, which creditors hold the debt, its cost and terms, debt service against exports and revenue, upcoming payments, debt flows, arrears and reserves, and comparisons with peers. Covers which measure answers each part, the traps in each, and what an external-only profile leaves out. Load for questions about a country's debt situation, how much it owes and to whom, how expensive its debt is, or what it pays each year. Questions about whether the debt is sustainable or at risk need the debt-sustainability skill as well.
debt-profile.name: debt-profile

debt-sustainability.description: Context on how the IMF and World Bank assess whether a country's public debt is sustainable, and how far public data can approximate their assessments. Covers debt sustainability analyses (DSAs), which of the two frameworks applies to a country (the joint framework for low-income countries, LIC-DSF, or the IMF's framework for market-access countries, MAC-SRDSF), risk ratings against sustainability judgements, solvency against liquidity, the indicators and thresholds each framework uses, and why indicators built from debt and macroeconomic data differ from a DSA's. Carries the IMF's list of LIC DSAs with each country's latest risk of external debt distress. Load for questions about whether a country's debt is sustainable, its risk of debt distress or sovereign stress, which countries are at high risk or in debt distress, default risk, DSA ratings, debt thresholds or the debt sustainability frameworks.
debt-sustainability.name: debt-sustainability
